19 A cable on a suspension bridge supports a weight of 19.3 × 105
N. This weight causes the cable
to stretch by 47 mm.
A lorry crossing the bridge then increases the force on the cable to 23.3 × 105
N. The
force-extension graph for the cable is shown.
23.3 × 105
force / N
19.3 × 105
0
0
47
57
extension / mm
What is the increase in strain energy in the cable when the lorry is crossing the bridge?
A
21 kJ
B
23 kJ
C
45 kJ
D
66 kJ

hints: Notice the graph gives two points: $19.3 \times 10^5 \text{ N}$ at $47 \text{ mm}$ and $23.3 \times 10^5 \text{ N}$ at $57 \text{ mm}$.
Recall strain energy is the area under the force-extension graph, so the increase is only the strip between $47 \text{ mm}$ and $57 \text{ mm}$.
Calculate the area of that trapezium with width $(57-47) \text{ mm} = 0.010 \text{ m}$ and average force $0.5 \times (F_1+F_2)$.
walkthrough: Identify the change from the graph: extension increases from $x_1 = 47 \text{ mm} = 0.047 \text{ m}$ to $x_2 = 57 \text{ mm} = 0.057 \text{ m}$ while force rises from $F_1 = 19.3 \times 10^5 \text{ N}$ to $F_2 = 23.3 \times 10^5 \text{ N}$.
State the rule: elastic strain energy equals area under the force-extension graph, so the increase is the area under the line between $x_1$ and $x_2$.
For a straight line this strip is a trapezium of width $\Delta x = 0.057 - 0.047 = 0.010 \text{ m}$ and average height $F_{av} = 0.5(F_1+F_2)$.
Multiply by width: $\Delta E = 21.3 \times 10^5 \times 0.010 = 2.13 \times 10^4 \text{ J} \approx 21 \text{ kJ}$.

A.explanation: Increase is the trapezium area between 47 mm and 57 mm, $0.5 \times (19.3+23.3) \times 10^5 \times 0.010 \approx 21 \times 10^3 \text{ J}$.

B.explanation: About $23 \text{ kJ}$ does not match the area between the two extensions; it is close to but larger than the correct trapezium area.

C.explanation: About $45 \text{ kJ}$ is the initial stored energy $0.5 \times 19.3 \times 10^5 \times 0.047$, not the increase.

D.explanation: About $66 \text{ kJ}$ is the final total energy $0.5 \times 23.3 \times 10^5 \times 0.057$, not the increase.
